b: Young Americans are dating less and getting married later, if at all. And sometimes the sexes don’t even seem to like each other much. What’s separating men and women, and leading to a decline in romance? And what can be done to reverse it?

My guest today did extensive polling research and conducted over one hundred hours of interviews with young adults to find out. His name is Daniel Cox, and he’s the director of the Survey Center on American Life and the author of Generation Uncoupled.

Today on the show, Daniel explains why young adults have become more hesitant about dating and marriage, how social media has distorted men’s and women’s perceptions of each other, and why dating apps haven’t delivered on their promise. We also discuss why the romance recession is really downstream of the friendship recession, and Daniel explains how the size of a man’s social circle is strongly connected to his dating prospects, why young people need more opportunities to take interpersonal risks, and how rebuilding all kinds of relationships is the key to reviving romantic ones.
This article was originally published on The Art of Manliness.
